To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multimodal handwashing campaign was effective in improving HCW hand hygiene rates in a low-income country.

a multimodal hand-hygiene campaign significantly improved hand-hygiene compliance among health care workers (HCWs) in a hospital in Addis Abba, Ethiopia, and that HCWs were more likely to perform hand hygiene when commercial hand sanitizer was available.

there was a significant increase (p < 0.0001) in hand hygiene adherence (from 2.1 to 12.8) among Ethiopian health care workers following the implementation of an abbreviated multimodal hand hygiene intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of a WHO-recommendation multimodal hand hygiene intervention in Ethiopia and the challenges that were encountered.
the impact of a hand hygiene campaign in a resource-limited setting.
the implementation of hand hygiene campaigns and the barriers to hand hygiene adherence, and provides a model for future hand hygiene campaigns in resource-limited environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WHO hand hygiene campaign was effective in improving HCW hand hygiene in our setting.
the implementation of a multimodal WHO hand hygiene campaign was associated with a significant increase in adherence to hand hygiene among Ethiopian HCWs.

hand hygiene adherence can be improved in resource-limited setting through implementation of a WHO recommended multimodal hand hygiene intervention, however, the use of commercial hand sanitizer should be considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a WHO-recommended hand hygiene campaign is effective at improving hand hygiene adherence, but that further work is needed to improve the WHO formulation of hand sanitizer.
the implementation of a multimodal WHO hand hygiene campaign is an effective strategy for promoting HCW hand hygiene and that commercial alcohol-based hand rubs are preferred by HCWs in our setting.
hand hygiene adherence in a resource-limited setting can be significantly improved by a WHO-recommended hand hygiene campaign.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hand hygiene adherence can be improved in resource limited settings, but that further research is required to identify the most effective hand hygiene products for use in resource limited settings.
a multimodal hand washing campaign can improve adherence to hand hygiene in resource-limited setting and that the WHO formulation for hand sanitizer is not optimal for resource-limited settings.
a multimodal handwashing campaign can be successfully implemented in resource-limited setting and can be a useful tool in improving hand hygiene compliance.
